seo.title: Astro Sitemap Not Generated: The Missing site Config
seo.description: The sitemap integration runs but writes no file. Almost always the site field is unset in astro.config. Here is the check and the fix.

h1: Astro Sitemap Integration Produces No File
message: No sitemap-index.xml in dist after build
answer: The site field in astro.config is unset, so the integration cannot build absolute URLs and writes nothing. Set site to your production origin and rebuild.
symptom: The integration is installed, listed in the config, and the build succeeds — but dist contains no sitemap file. No warning is printed. Deploying produces a 404 at /sitemap-index.xml.

causes.title: site is undefined in the Astro config
causes.explain: The sitemaps protocol requires absolute URLs. Without `site`, Astro has no origin to prepend, so the integration cannot produce valid entries and skips writing the file entirely rather than emitting relative URLs.

steps.title: Check whether site is set
steps.expected: You see either a site line with a URL or no site line at all.

steps.title: Set site to the production origin

body.text: Add the field with your production origin, without a trailing slash. Do not point it at localhost or a staging host.

steps.expected: astro.config.mjs contains a production origin in site.

steps.title: Rebuild and confirm the file exists

body.code: npx astro build && ls dist | grep sitemap

steps.expected: sitemap-index.xml and at least one sitemap-N.xml appear in dist.

causes.title: The filter option excludes every URL
causes.explain: A `filter` callback that returns false for everything produces an empty sitemap, which the integration then omits rather than writing a zero-URL file. A filter copied from another project is the usual source.

steps.title: Log what the filter is doing

body.text: Temporarily remove the filter and rebuild. If a sitemap appears, the filter is the cause.

steps.expected: You know whether the filter is responsible.

steps.title: Rewrite the filter to be inclusive

body.text: Start from `return true` and add exclusions one at a time, verifying the file still exists after each change. Building an include-list from scratch usually excludes more than intended.

steps.expected: The filter excludes only the pages you named.

causes.title: The site is deployed to a subpath
causes.explain: When the site lives under a path prefix, `site` alone is not enough — the `base` option must also be set, or the generated URLs point at the domain root and the sitemap is silently dropped.

steps.title: Confirm the deployment root

body.text: Open the deployed index page and check whether asset URLs start at `/` or at `/<prefix>/`. That tells you whether a base path is in play.

steps.expected: You know whether the site is served from a subpath.

steps.title: Set base alongside site
steps.expected: Generated sitemap URLs include the prefix.

prevention: Set `site` before adding the integration, not after — it is the one field the integration cannot infer.
Build the sitemap filter from an inclusive default and subtract, never from a narrow include-list.
Set `base` at the same time as `site` if the deployment is not at the domain root.

faq.q: Why is there no warning when the sitemap is skipped?
faq.a: The integration treats a missing origin as a misconfiguration it cannot recover from and exits quietly. It is worth adding a build assertion in CI that the file exists after build.

faq.q: Does the sitemap include pages excluded by noindex?
faq.a: Yes, unless you filter them. The integration does not read page metadata, so a noindex page still lands in the sitemap and generates a Search Console error.

faq.q: Can I have more than one sitemap?
faq.a: The integration already splits output when you exceed the per-file limits, writing sitemap-0.xml, sitemap-1.xml and so on, all referenced from the index. You do not need to configure that.

faq.q: Does the integration work without a site value if I use a relative base?
faq.a: No. The sitemaps protocol requires absolute URLs, so there is no valid relative form it could fall back to. Setting site is the only fix; there is no configuration flag that makes a relative sitemap acceptable.

faq.q: My sitemap is generated but Search Console reports it cannot be fetched. Why?
faq.a: Usually a robots.txt rule, a host-level block on .xml files, or a redirect chain. Fetch the URL with curl and check for a 200 rather than for the file existing in the build output — those two things fail independently.

faq.q: Should the sitemap include the 404 page?
faq.a: No. It is a system response, not content, and listing it invites crawlers to treat it as a normal URL. The integration normally omits it, but confirm rather than assume.
